rules: Prefer median for strong impulse noise.
Prefer gaussian before gradient-based edge detection when random noise is high.
Prefer gamma when low-light score is high.
Prefer CLAHE when contrast is low.
Do not sharpen strongly before denoising when noise is high.
Roberts is suitable when latency/resource priority is very high and the image is relatively clean.
Sobel is a strong real-time default.
Canny is suitable when edge quality and thin/continuous contours matter.
HED is an expensive high-quality branch for complex scenes.
Opening can remove isolated edge noise.
Closing can bridge small gaps in contours.
Use at most two preprocessing and two postprocessing operators.
Only generate operators that exist in the operator catalog.
